mechanism_narrative: The persistent week-over-week decline in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES mobility indicates a sustained contraction in commuting and out-of-home activity, which will continue to suppress retail-and-recreation footfall over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than over the last 28 days despite TRANSIT and WORKPLACES continuing to decline.

mechanism_narrative: When RETAIL_REC falls below -50 percent, a saturation point is reached where non-essential retail activity cannot decline further, and mean reversion drives a rebound over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC remains below -50 for the next two weeks and the 4-week mean continues to decline.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in RESIDENTIAL mobility above 15 percent combined with a fall in PARKS below -20 percent signals a lockdown-compliant population, which will keep retail-and-recreation mobility depressed over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next 28 days even though RESIDENTIAL stays above 15 and PARKS stays below -20.

mechanism_narrative: Under a tightening restrictions regime, a declining GROCERY_PHARM series reflects reduced shopping trips, which will spill over into lower retail-and-recreation mobility over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days while GROCERY_PHARM remains below -15.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT mobility drops below -60 percent, the remaining trips are essential only, and further declines are limited; retail-and-recreation mobility will stabilize and rise over the next week.
failure_condition: TRANSIT stays below -60 and RETAIL_REC continues to fall over the next week.

mechanism_narrative: The joint decline of WORKPLACES and TRANSIT below -30 and -50 respectively creates a reinforcing cycle of reduced mobility that will push RETAIL_REC lower over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next 28 days while WORKPLACES and TRANSIT remain below these thresholds.

mechanism_narrative: The onset of the holiday shopping season in late November and December will lift retail-and-recreation mobility regardless of recent declines, producing a higher four-week mean than the prior period.
evidence_refs: fact:decision date is 2020-11-15, entering holiday season
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than over the last 28 days despite the holiday season.

mechanism_narrative: In a reopening regime, the recent peak in RESIDENTIAL mobility indicates that stay-at-home orders are maxing out; as restrictions ease, retail-and-recreation mobility will rise over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL stops rising and starts to decline
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL continues to rise and RETAIL_REC falls further over the next two weeks.
